questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is a naturally occurring growth inhibitor?
questions.solution: Abscisic acid (ABA) is a growth inhibitor and are produced in plants during abscission. IAA, NAA and GA are growth promoters inducing cell division.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: You are given tissue with its potential for differentiation in artificial culture. Which of the following pairs of hormones would you add to the medium to secure shoots as well as roots?
questions.solution: Auxins and cytokinins are used in the development of root and shoot in a culture medium (respectively).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Differentiation of shoot is controlled by
questions.solution: In tissue culture, differentiation of shoot is controlled by high cytokinin: auxin ratio, while high auxin: cytokinin ratio is responsible for root formation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Phototropic and geotropic movements are linked to
questions.solution: Phototropic movements are the plant responses towards the light. Generally, plant shoot and flower show positive phototropism while geotropism is the plant response to the gravity of earth. Generally, roots are positively geotropic. Auxin is the phytohormone which induces apical dominance and phototropic movements.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: ABA is involved in
questions.solution: Abscisic acid acts as a growth inhibitor and induces dormancy of buds towards the approach of winter. Dormancy of seeds is mainly caused by abscisic acid. Because of its action in inducing dormancy abscisic acid (ABA) is also called dormin. The buds, as well as seeds, sprout only when abscisic acid is overcome by gibberellins.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Photoperiodic stimulus is received by
questions.solution: Photoperiodic stimulus is perceived by mature-old leaves.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Parthenocarpy is induced by
questions.solution: In the presence of auxins unfertilized ovary gets changed into a fruit.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Senescence in plants is inhibited by
questions.solution: Cytokinin delays the senescence (ageing) of leaves and other organs by controlling protein synthesis and mobilization of resources (Disappearance of chlorophyll). It is called the Richmond-Lang effect. It was reported by Richmond and Lang (1957) while working on detached leaves of Xanthium.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
How many of the following tissues given below are formed by dedifferentiation?

[Intra-fascicular cambium, inter-fascicular cambium, cork cambium, procambium, phelloderm]
questions.solution: Dedifferentiation is the process in which permanent tissue like parenchyma regains the power of division and becomes meristematic, such meristem is called secondary meristems like inter-fascicular cambium and cork cambium.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Auxin increases the __________ of cell walls.
questions.solution: Auxin is known to elongate the cell. It causes certain changes across the membrane such that cellulase enzyme cause loosening of the fibers of the cell wall. Loosening of fiber increase the plasticity of the cell wall.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: One set of plants was grown at 12 hours day and 12 hours night period cycles, and it flowered. While in the other set, the night phase was interrupted by the flash of light and did not produce flowers. Under which one of the following categories will you place this plant?
questions.solution: Short-day plants require long uninterrupted dark period for flowering. They will not produce flower if night was interrupted by flash of light. In these plants, flowering takes place after exposure to a photoperiod shorter than their critical photoperiod.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Pneumatophores are seen in
questions.solution: In some plants such as Rhizophora, growing in swampy areas, many roots come out of the ground and grow vertically upwards. Such roots, called pneumatophores, help to get oxygen for respiration.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is incorrect about plant hormones?
options: They influence plant growth and development at low concentrations.
Abscisic acid is growth retarding hormone
Ethylene decreases the respiration rate in fruits.
questions.solution: Ethylene is highly effective in fruit ripening. It enhances the respiration rate during the ripening of the fruits. This rise in the rate of respiration is called respiratory climactic.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following hormone, in combination with auxin, stimulates cell division in plants and determines the course of differentiation mainly?
questions.solution: The cytokinin hormones promote cell division and tissue growth and depend upon the presence of auxins to determine the extent of their activity. When the ratio of cytokinins to auxins is relatively high, stem and leaf growth is stimulated. Auxins and cytokinins are the best documented as impinging directly on cell cycle control.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
questions.solution: Gibberellic acid is a growth promoter thus it inhibits leaf fall. Abscisic acid is commonly called stress hormone and it promotes closure of stomata. Cytokinin promotes cell division. IAA is an auxin that induces cell elongation and cell division resulting in plant growth and development.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: When all parts except the leaves of a short-day plant are covered with a light-proof cover and then subjected to short daylight/dark treatment, it will produce flower buds. When a portion of this plant is grafted on to another plant of the same species which has been prevented from flowering by excessive exposure to light, this latter plant will also produce flower buds. Which is the best inference from this result?
options: Hormones can transmit information to all parts of plants
Leaves are more sensitive to the photoperiodic stimulus than other parts of the plant
The photoperiodic stimulus is received by the leaves and transmitted by a hormone.
The photoperiodic stimulus is received by all parts of the shoot and transmitted by a hormone.
questions.solution:
Auxin hormone is responsible for photoperiodism.
The photoperiodic stimulus is received by the leaves and transmitted by auxin hormone.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following hormones can replace vernalization?
questions.solution: The stimulus of vernalization in known as vernalin. The stimulus of vernalization that induces flowering could be particular gibberellin or a mixture of gibberellins.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: <u>                   </u> is used to speed up the malting process in the brewing industry.
questions.solution: GA<sub>3</sub> is used to speed up the malting process in brewing industry.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In tissue culture experiments of tobacco callus, it was seen that when the culture medium contains 2 ppm of IAA and 2 ppm of kinetin, an undifferentiated mass of callus is produced. If the ratio of kinetin to IAA is increased, then
options: The callus size would increase by repeated cell divisions
questions.solution:
Kinetin causes organogenesis in tissue culture.
Kinetin is a type of cytokinin, a class of plant hormone that promotes cell division. Kinetin was originally isolated by Miller and Skoog et al. as a compound from autoclaved herring sperm DNA that had cell division-promoting activity.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which kind of plants are required for uninterrupted dark-period flowering?
questions.solution: A plant that flowers only after being exposed to light periods shorter than a certain critical length, as in early spring or fall. Chrysanthemums and strawberries are short-day plants. uninterrupted darkness triggers flowering in short-day plants

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Zeatin has been obtained from
questions.solution:
Search for natural substances with cytokinin-like activities led to the isolation of zeatin from corn-kernels and coconut milk.
For the first time, zeatin was obtained from corn milk by Letham in 1963.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is used for bolting in beet?
questions.solution: Gibberellins are PGR which are acidic in nature and have been reported from widely different organisms such as fungi and higher plants. They are denoted as GA<sub>1</sub>, GA<sub>2</sub>, GA<sub>3</sub> and so on. They produce a wide range of physiological responses in plants. Their ability to cause an increase in the length of the axis is used to increase the length of grapes stalks. Gibberellins, cause fruits like apple to elongate and improve its shape. They also delay senescence. Gibberellins also promote bolting (internode elongation just prior to flowering) in beet, cabbages and many plants with rosette habit.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Genetic dwarfness in plants can be resolved by
questions.solution: One of the most striking effects of gibberellins is the elongation of genetic dwarf (mutant) varieties of plants like corn and pea. It is believed that dwarfism in the mutant variety of plant is due to blocking of the capacity for normal gibberellin production (deficiency of gibberellin). When gibberellin is applied to single gene dwarf mutants they grow to their normal heights.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following would occur during bolting?
questions.solution: Gibberellins promote bolting (internode elongation just prior to flowering) in beet, cabbages, and many plants with rosette habit.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Shoot apices those modify themselves into flowering apices, cannot perceive photoperiods.
Sugarbeet, cabbage and carrots are monocarpic plants.
To initiate flowering, LDP must be exposed to light for a period less than critical duration.
Ethephon causes thinning of cotton, cherry & walnut.
questions.solution: Long Day Plants (LDP) requires exposure to light for a period exceeding critical duration to induce flowering. Ethephon hastens fruit ripening in tomatoes and apples and accelerates abscission in flowers and fruits (thinning of cotton, cherry, walnut). Shoot apices those modify themselves into flowering apices, cannot perceive photoperiods. Biennial monocarpic plants that flower and then die in the second season. Some examples are sugar beet, cabbage, carrot, etc

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Apical dominance in higher plants is due to
questions.solution: Presence of auxin causes apical dominance in plants and cytokinins are responsible for breaking of apical dominance.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Nicotiana sylvestris flowers only during long days and N. tabacum flowers only during short days. If raised in the laboratory under different photoperiods, they can be induced to flower at the same time and can be cross-fertilized to produce self-fertile offspring. What is the best reason for considering N. sylvestris and N. tabacum to be separate species?
questions.solution: The term species evolves from word specific means only those groups of plants or animals come under one species which can interbreed and produce fertile offsprings naturally. N. tabacum and N. sylvestris cannot produce flowers naturally have different photoperiods, hence they cannot belong to the same species. Thus, they cannot interbreed in nature.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which combination of gases is suitable for fruit ripening?
questions.solution: Ethylene acts physiologically as a hormone in plants. It stimulates the ripening of fruit, the opening of flowers, and the abscission (or shedding) of leaves. Its biosynthesis starts from methionine with 1-arninocyclopropane-1-carboxylic acid (ACC) as a key intermediate.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The ageing of leaves is called
questions.solution: The ageing of leaves is called senescence. It is the process of growing old, which occurs in all species and is typified by a gradual slowing down of metabolism and breakdown of tissues, often accompanied by endocrinal changes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Attractive force of cell walls of xylem for water molecules is termed as
questions.solution: Walls of tracheids and vessels of xylem are made up of lignin and cellulose and have a strong affinity for water (adhesion).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Ethylene is highly effective in fruit ripening. It enhances the respiration rate during ripening of fruits, this rise in rate of respiration is called
questions.solution: Ethylene promotes senescence and abscission of plant organs especially of leaves and flowers. Ethylene is highly effective in fruit ripening. It enhances the respiration rate during ripening of the fruits. This rise in rate of respiration is called respiratory climactic.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Gibberellin was first extracted from
questions.solution: Gibberellins was extracted from rice seedling suffering from 'bakanae disease' which is caused by Gibberella fujikuroi fungus.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: There are two plants A and B with respective critical photoperiod of 13 hours and 11 hours. When they are exposed to light for a period of 12 hours, it initiated flowering in both. Which of the following conclusions is most appropriate for these plants?
options: Both plant A and B are long day plants
Both plant A and B are short day plants
Plant A is short day plant and plant B is long day plant
Plant A is long day plant and plant B is short day plant
questions.solution: Plant A is a short-day plant (A plant that flowers only after being exposed to light periods shorter than a certain critical length.) and plant B is a long-day plant (A plant that flowers only after being exposed to light periods longer than a certain critical length).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Arithmetic growth curve is represented by which of the following equation?
questions.solution: In arithmetic growth, one of the daughter cells continues to divide, whereas the other differentiates into maturity following mitotic cell division. The rate of growth is constant and increase in growth occurs in arithmetic progression, i.e., 1,2,3,4,5 and so on. questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The habit of a cabbage or acaulescent plant can be changed drastically by the application of
questions.solution: Gibberellins promote bolting (internode elongation just prior to flowering) in beet, cabbages and many plants with rosette habit.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Turgor pressure becomes equal to the wall pressure when
options: No exchange of water takes place
Solute goes from the cell into water
questions.solution: When turgor pressure is equal to the wall pressure the establishment of equilibrium (isotonic solution) takes place between the solution, and hence osmosis doesn't take place.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In progressive senescence, the leaves fall
questions.solution: The progressive senescence is a developmentary process which ultimately leads to complete loss of organization and function of the plant.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which plant hormone is related to hastening the maturity period and germination of seeds?
questions.solution: Gibberellin cause seeds germination by activating vegetative growth of the embryo and mobilizing stored food reserve of the endosperm by promoting the synthesis of hydrolytic enzymes involved in the solubilisation of endosperm reserve. Spraying juvenile conifers with gibberellins hastens the maturity period, thus leading to early seed production.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Seed and bud dormancy can be induced by
questions.solution: Abscisic acid (ABA) acts as a growth inhibitor and induces dormancy of buds towards the approach of winter. Dormancy of seeds is mainly caused by abscisic acid. Because of its role in inducing dormancy, abscisic acid is also called as dormin. The buds as well as seeds sprout only when the concentration of abscisic acid is overcome by gibberellins.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following is a set of natural growth regulators?
questions.solution: Plant growth regulators are growth promoter and growth inhibitors. Those which are naturally synthesized by plants are natural growth regulators. Certain chemical substance when applied to plants shows similar effect and are reffered as synthetic hormone.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Two important intrinsic controls which are important in plant growth and development are
questions.solution: Plant growth regulators (PGRs) or phytohormones control growth and development of plants and play an important role along with genomic control. PGRs can be growth promoters or inhibitors.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Select the incorrect statements.
options: ABA acts as antagonist to GAs.
Ethylene can act both as a promotor and an inhibitor of growth activity.
Auxin and ethylene promotes apical dominance.
questions.solution: ABA is a growth inhibitor which inhibits seed germination and promotes seed dormancy. It acts opposite or antagonistic to GAs. Ethylene is promoter at low concentration but at high concentration it function as inhibitor. Ethylene is synergistic with auxin at low concentration and promotes apical dominance.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Select the odd one with respect to long-day plants.
questions.solution: The term long-day describes plants that begin forming flower buds when the days are longer than their critical day length (e.g., spinach, wheat, radish, beet, lettuce, mentha, poppy are examples of long-day plants). Sunflower is a day-neutral plant.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
The following statements are given about different plant growth hormones:

I. Cytokinin suppresses the synthesis of chlorophyll.
II. Auxins control apical dominance.
III. Gibberellins promote shoot elongation.
IV. Abscisic acid enables seeds to withstand desiccation.

Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution: 'Cytokinin' delays the senescence of leaves and prevents chlorophyll degradation. It can be shown by a rapid bioassay technique. Cytokinin treated leaf tips retard the process of chlorophyll degradation as compared to untreated leaf discs.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is correct about vernalization?
options: Flowering is only quantitatively dependent on low temperature.
It is seen in the biennial plants
questions.solution: There are plants for which flowering is either quantitatively or qualitatively dependent on exposure to low temperature. This phenomenon is termed vernalisation. It prevents precocious reproductive development late in the growing season and enables the plant to have sufficient time to reach maturity. Vernalization is seen in biennial plants. Biennials are monocarpic plants that normally flower and die in the second season. Sugarbeet, cabbages and carrots are some of the common biennials. Subjecting the growing of a biennial plant to a cold treatment stimulates a subsequent photoperiodic flowering response.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Cytokinins were discovered as
questions.solution: Kinetin (a modified form of adenine, a purine) is obtained from the autoclaved herring sperm DNA. Kinetin does not occur naturally in plants. Search for natural substances with cytokinin-like activities led to the isolation of zeatin from corn-kernels and coconut milk. Since the discovery of zeatin, several naturally occurring cytokinins and some synthetic compounds with cell division promoting activity have been identified. Natural cytokinins are synthesized in regions where rapid cell division occurs, for example, root apices, developing shoot buds, young fruits, etc.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The site of perception of light/dark duration are the
questions.solution: Leaves of plants consist of a pigment system known as phytochrome which perceives light and controls photoperiodic induction. Phytochrome occurs in two interconvertible forms which regulate gene activity and production of flowering hormone florigen.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: One of the effects of Gibberellins is to induce the synthesis of amylase enzyme which causes the break down of starch and provides nourishment to the embryo in the seed. This phenomenon leads to the germination of seed. The hormone antagonist to this phenomenon is
questions.solution: ABA acts as a general plant growth inhibitor and an inhibitor of plant metabolism. ABA inhibits seed germination. ABA stimulates the closure of stomata and increases the tolerance of plants to various kinds of stresses. Therefore, it is also called the stress hormone. ABA plays an important role in seed development, maturation and dormancy. By inducing dormancy, ABA helps seeds to withstand desiccation and other factors unfavourable for growth.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following hormones is not found in plants?
questions.solution: <math><mn>2,4</mn><mo>–</mo><mi>D</mi></math> is the synthetic or exogenous auxin. 2,4-Dichlorophenoxyacetic acid (usually called 2,4-D) is an organic compound with the chemical formula C<sub>8</sub>H<sub>6</sub>Cl<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>. It is a systemic herbicide which selectively kills most broadleaf weeds by causing uncontrolled growth in them, but it leaves most grasses such as cereals, lawn turf and grassland relatively unaffected.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Cell wall thickening, protoplasmic modification, and functional specialization are observed in which phase of growth?
questions.solution: The phase of maturation is the most important phase in which the cell becomes structurally and functionally specialized and differentiate to form a different type of cells and then tissue. Cell wall material deposition is the most important process which determines the functional specialty of the cell.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Find the odd one out from the options showing certain auxins.
questions.solution: Auxins are plant growth promoters responsible for apical dominance. 2,4-D or 2,4- dichlorophenoxyacetic acid is a synthetic auxin. IAA, IBA, and NAA are naturally occurring auxins.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: If an agronomist is trying to induce flowering in a short-day plant and unknowingly it gets exposed to light for some amount of time. What will be the consequence of this plant?
options: It will resume its cycle and induce flower.
questions.solution: Short day plants will only flower if they are exposed to a short period of daylight and long periods of darkness. If the dark period is interrupted, the plant will not flower. Hence, short-day plants are also called long night plants, e.g., rice, soyabean, etc.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The growth of the given system per unit time expressed on a common basis, per unit initial parameter is called
questions.solution: The growth of the given system per unit time expressed on a common basis, e.g., per unit initial parameter is called the relative growth rate. The relative growth rate is determined by the growth of the plant in its size at certain time intervals.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the given statements about auxins and state whether they are true or false:

a. Auxin promotes apical dominance.
b. Auxins have a negative impact on cytokinin levels.
c. F.W. Went isolated auxins from the coleoptiles of the oat plant.
d. Auxin promotes flowering in the pineapple plants.
questions.solution: F.W. Went isolated the auxins from the Avena coleoptiles. Auxins promote apical dominance by inhibiting the growth of lateral buds. Auxins promote flowering in plants like pineapple as it is a growth-promoting hormone-like cytokinin. Auxins do not affect the cytokinin level negatively as they are not antagonistic in function.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following phytohormones are used to hasten the process of maturation in conifers?
questions.solution: Gibberellin is one of the growth hormones which promotes growth by inducing elongation in the axis of the plant. It has effects like longer leaves, long internodes, etc.  Spraying juvenile conifers with GAs hastens the maturity period, thus leading to early seed production.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Growth of vascular cambium is an example of:
questions.solution:
In arithmetic growth, the cell divides giving rise to two daughter cells. From which, only one daughter cell continues to divide while the other differentiates and matures to become a permanent cell. This kind of nature of growth rate is shown by meristematic cells.

Plasticity is the ability of the tissues to form different structures in response to environmental conditions. Senescence is the deterioration phase with respect to the ageing of a cell or tissue or an organism.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The specific property attributed to gibberellins is
questions.solution: Gibberellins are weakly acidic hormones having gibbane ring structure which cause cell elongation of intact plants in general and increased internodal length of genetically dwarfed plants (i.e., corn, pea) in particular.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Early fruit drop can be avoided by spraying
questions.solution: Generally, it is observed that intact fruits do not fall as they synthesize auxin. Abscission occurs when the auxin content falls below a minimum point. Hence, the application of auxin to the plants slows the abscission of leaves, fruits, branches, etc. The premature drop of fruits, such as apple, pear and citrus, can be prevented to a great extent by spraying the trees with a dilute solution of IAA, NAA.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statement is false with respect to the application of auxins?
options: Control direction of growth of plants
Initiate and promote cell division actively particularly in tissue culture
questions.solution: Cytokinin initiates and promotes cell division actively in plant tissue and cell culture. Auxins are basically used for the formation of callus (an undifferentiated mass of cells).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Chemically, auxin is
questions.solution: Auxin is indole-<math><mn>3</mn></math> Acetic Acid. It is formed from amino acid tryptophan. Cytokinins are amino purine and also named as kinetin. Gibberellins are diterpenes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A modified form of adenine, a purine
options: was discovered from autoclaved herring sperm DNA
is naturally found in plants and helps in preventing apical dominance
was isolated from corn kernels and coconut milk
is a synthetic compound which promotes cell division in plants
questions.solution: N6-furfurylamino purine is a modified form of adenine called kinetin. It was discovered from autoclaved herring sperm DNA. It is not naturally found in plants. It has cytokinin activity and used in plant tissue culture along with low auxin to promote the formation of the stem in callus. Zeatin was isolated from corn kernels and coconut milk.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Mark the correct statement/s about arithmetic growth.
options: In mitosis, only one daughter cell continues to divide while the other differentiates and matures.
The simplest expression of this growth is exemplified by a root elongating at a constant rate.
questions.solution:
In arithmetic growth, following mitotic cell division, only one daughter cell continues to divide while the other differentiates and matures. The simplest expression of arithmetic growth is exemplified by a root elongating at a constant rate. Look at Figure 15.5. On plotting the length of the organ against time, a linear curve is obtained. Mathematically, it is expressed as
Lt = L0 + rt
Lt = length at time ‘t’
L0 = length at time ‘zero’
r = growth rate / elongation per unit time.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Where would you look for active cell division in plants?
options: At the tip of root and shoot
questions.solution: In the apical meristem tissue, actively dividing cells are present.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In humans, the activation of sympathetic nervous system stimulates the adrenal medulla to release certain hormones that help in flight and fight response. A similar type of response in plants can be given by
questions.solution: Abscisic acid (ABA) is an inhibitory plant hormone also known as 'dormin' hormone as it promotes seed dormancy and inhibits growth. ABA is a stress hormone as it helps the plant survive different kinds of environmental stresses. It also stimulates the closure of stomata. It acts as the antagonist of the gibberellic acid.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Substances which originate at the tip of the stem and control growth elsewhere are
questions.solution: Hormones are secreted by cells in one part of the plant and produce their effect in other part of the plant.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Respiratory climactic is brought about by which of the following hormones?
questions.solution: Ethylene is highly effective in fruit ripening. It enhances the respiration rate during the ripening of the fruits. This rise in the rate of respiration is called respiratory climactic.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following shows plasticity?
options: More than one option is correct
questions.solution: Plants follow different pathways in response to the environment or phases of life to form different kinds of structures. This ability is called plasticity, e.g., heterophylly in cotton, coriander and larkspur. In such plants, the leaves of the juvenile plant are different in shape from those in mature plants. On the other hand, differences in shapes of leaves produced in air and those produced in water in buttercup also represent the heterophyllous development due to the environment. This phenomenon of heterophylly is an example of plasticity.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A potted plant placed near the window bends outwardly due to
options: Greater oxygen availability to the tip
More auxin content on the shaded side
Availability of necessary warmth to the tip
questions.solution: Greater growth of the shaded side of the stem is due to more accumulation of auxin on the shaded side than on the illuminated side.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is correct about flowering in rice and wheat plants?
options: Rice needs a continuous uninterrupted long period of light to flower while wheat needs a continuous uninterrupted long period of darkness to flower
Wheat needs a continuous uninterrupted long period of light to flower while rice needs a continuous uninterrupted long period of darkness to flower
Both rice and wheat need a continuous uninterrupted long period of light to flower
Both rice and wheat need a continuous uninterrupted long period of darkness to flower
questions.solution:
Wheat is a long day plant. These plants flowers only when they exposed to critical photoperiod or photoperiod longer than their critical day length. They need a continuous (uninterrupted) light period for flowering.

Rice is a short day or long night plant. These plants give flowers on exposure to photoperiod equal to or shorter than their critical day length. They need a continuous (uninterrupted) dark period for flowering.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following information about a phytohormone and then identify it.

I. They cause fruits like apple to elongate and improve their shape.
II. They are used to speed up the malting process in the brewing industry.
III. They are used to convert genetically dwarf plants into tall plants.
questions.solution: Gibberellins are growth promoter phytohormones. They are denoted as GA1, GA2 and GA3, and so on. Gibberellic acid (GA3) was one of the first gibberellins to be discovered and remains the most intensively studied form. Gibberellins cause fruits like apple to elongate and improve its shape. They also delay senescence. GA3 is used to speed up the malting process in the brewing industry. They also cause internode elongation, and hence, they can be used to convert a dwarf plant into a tall plant.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
The following experiment was performed to test the effect of auxin on the plant growth. Five plant seedlings (all growing actively) were prepared as below; they were unilaterally illuminated, and growth was measured after 10 days.

Treatments :

Plant A: Tip not removed, nothing applied
Plant B: Tip removed, nothing applied
Plant C: Tip removed, gelatin block with cytokinin was placed on the cut edge
Plant D: Tip removed gelatin block with auxin placed on the cut edge.

Which of the following plants would show curvature after the above treatment?
questions.solution: Auxin is the plant hormone that is synthesized in young stem apex. During day time, auxin redistribution occurs such that the plant side directly exposed to sunlight contains lower auxin concentration than the other side which is not exposed to light. This unequal distribution causes curvature. In plant A, redistribution of auxin leads to curvature, whereas removal of the tip in plant B leads to no auxin synthesis and no curvature. However, in plant D, where gelatine box with auxin is placed due to auxin redistribution, the curvature is observed.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In the below diagrams, A and B are initial areas of leaves. A' and B' are areas of leaves after growth. Which of the following is correct?
options: Both relative and absolute growth of leaves are same
Absolute growth is same, but relative growth is different
Absolute growth is different, but relative growth is the same
Both absolute and relative growth of leaves are different
questions.solution:
Quantitative comparisons between the growth of a living system can also be made in two ways: (i) measurement and the comparison of total growth per unit time is called the absolute growth rate. (ii) The growth of the given system per unit time expressed on a common basis, e.g., per unit initial parameter, is called the relative growth rate.
Here, absolute growth of leaf A to A’ is 2.5 cm2, whereas that of leaf B to B’ is 10cm2. Hence, absolute growth is different. Since 2.5 is 25% of 10, there is a total 25% increase in growth in leaf A, and in leaf B, 10 is 25% of 40, so there is also 25% increase in growth. Hence, the relative growth of two leaves is the same, that is 25%.

questions.solution: Vernalisation prevents precocious reproductive development late in the growing season and provides sufficient time to reach maturity.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In which of the following, plasticity can be seen due to the changing environment?
questions.solution: Plants follow different pathways in response to the environment or phases of life to form different kinds of structures. This ability is called plasticity, e.g., heterophylly in cotton, coriander and larkspur. In such plants, the leaves of the juvenile plant are different in shape from those in mature plants. On the other hand, differences in shapes of leaves produced in air and those produced in water in buttercup also represent the heterophyllous development due to the environment. This phenomenon of heterophylly is an example of plasticity.

questions.subject: Botany

In plant B, all floral buds are covered in such a way that no light can reach them but the leaves are exposed and light can reach them. Flowering will occur in plant B but not in plant A
Flowering will occur in both plant A as well as plant B
Flowering will not occur in both plant A as well as plant B

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is correct about seed dormancy?
options: The seed dormancy can be overcome by subjecting the seeds to warm conditions or by application of certain chemicals like gibberellic acid and nitrites.
An external environment like an impermeable and hard seed coat is responsible for inducing seed dormancy.
The presence of chemical inhibitors such as phenolic acids and para-ascorbic acid are internal factors that induce dormancy.
More than one option is correct.
questions.solution: Impermeable and hard seed coat; the presence of chemical inhibitors such as abscisic acids, phenolic acids, para-ascorbic acid; and immature embryos are some of the reasons which cause seed dormancy. Effect of inhibitory substances can be removed by subjecting the seeds to chilling conditions or by application of certain chemicals like gibberellic acid and nitrates.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: It takes a very long time for pineapple plants to produce flowers. Which combination of hormones can be applied to artificially induce flowering in pineapple plants throughout the year to increase yield?
questions.solution: The gibberellins, cytokinins and auxins are found to be growth stimulators, whereas ethylene and abscisic acid are determined as growth inhibitors. The function of cytokinin is the stimulation of cell division, growth of lateral buds and apical dominance. Functions of gibberellins are to stimulate stem elongation. Auxin and ethylene are responsible for the flowering and fruiting in pineapple.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: 2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid is used to eliminate _____ weeds from a ____ crop field.
questions.solution: Auxin, 2,4-Dichlorophenoxyacetic acid is used to kill dicotyledonous or broadleaf weeds. It does not affect mature monocotyledonous plants. It is used to prepare weed-free lawns by gardeners.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The hormone that can replace the process of vernalisation is
questions.solution: Vernalisation refers especially to the promotion of flowering by a period of low temperature. It prevents precocious reproductive development late in the growing season and enables the plant to have sufficient time to reach maturity. Gibberellins initiate growth in plants by stimulating cell elongation, and thereby, antagonistically, it regulates the process of vernalisation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Vernalization is defined as
options: all changes that an organism goes through during its life cycle.
flowering that is either quantitatively or qualitatively dependent on the exposure to low temperature.
flowering induced only when a plant is exposed to certain duration of photoperiod.
presence of different kinds of structure in response to environment or phases of life.
questions.solution: Vernalization is the induction of a plant's flowering process by exposure to the prolonged cold in winter or by an artificial equipment. After vernalization, plants acquire the ability to flower, but they may require additional seasonal cues or weeks of growth before they actually flower.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following option shows a pair of antagonist phytohormones with respect to the given feature?
options: Abscission: Ethylene antagonist to Abscisic acid

questions.solution: Both auxin and gibberellin can promote parthenocarpy. Both ethylene and abscisic acid promote abscission. Both gibberellin and cytokinin delay senescence. However, gibberellin promotes seed germination while Abscisic acid inhibits seed germination. Thus, they are antagonistic.

Promotion of male flowers in cucumbers thereby increasing its yield
Breaking the bud dormancy and promoting sprouting of potato tubers
Promotion of root growth and root hair formation, thus helping the plants to increase their absorption surface.

questions.solution: In most higher plants, the growing apical bud inhibits growth of the lateral buds; the phenomenon is called apical dominance. Removal of shoot tips (decapitation) usually results in the growth of lateral buds. It is widely applied in tea plantation and hedge making.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Opening of flower and drooping of a bud are
questions.solution: Nastic movements are non-directional movements in which the direction of response or movement is determined by the epinasty (greater growth on the adaxial side, e.g., the opening of flowers), hyponasty (greater growth on abaxial side e.g., closing of flowers), thigmotactic or chemonastic bending of tentacles in Drosera. questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:

I. Cytokinins induce cell division.
II. Cytokinins delay the onset of senescence.
III. Cytokinins initiate chloroplast formation in the presence of light.
IV. Application of cytokinins reduces the apical dominance and stimulates the growth of lateral buds.
questions.solution: Cytokinins induce cell division. They promote nutrient mobilisation which helps in the delay of leaf senescence. Cytokinins help overcome the apical dominance and in this aspect it is antagonistic to auxin.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The plant hormone that induces cell proliferation, plant growth and development, triggers callus differentiation, embryogenesis, maintenance of root and shoot meristems, keeps the cut flowers and vegetable fresh is
questions.solution: Cytokinins induce cell proliferation, trigger callus differentiation to shoot when applied with auxins, plant growth and development, embryogenesis, maintenance of root and shoot meristems. Cytokinins are sprayed to increase the shelf life of vegetables and cut flowers. The main reason behind this is that the cytokinin increases the retention of chlorophyll and delayed senescence in leaves.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is not the function of auxins?
questions.solution:
Auxins help to initiate rooting in stem cuttings, an application widely used for plant propagation. Auxins promote flowering e.g. in pineapples. They help to prevent fruit and leaf drop at early stages but promote the abscission of older mature leaves and fruits. In most higher plants, the growing apical bud inhibits the growth of the lateral (axillary) buds, a phenomenon called apical dominance. Auxins also induce parthenocarpy, e.g., in tomatoes. They are widely used as herbicides. 2, 4-D, widely used to kill dicotyledonous weeds, does not affect mature monocotyledonous plants. It is used to prepare weed-free lawns by gardeners. Auxin also controls xylem differentiation and helps in cell division.

Ethylene is responsible for the ripening of fruits.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The phenomenon of dedifferentiation is
options: regaining the capacity to divide mitotically by differentiated cells
the event of losing the ability to divide by dedifferentiated cells
regaining the capacity to divide meiotically by differentiated cells
regaining the capacity to divide meiotically by redifferentiated cells
questions.solution: The living differentiated cells that have lost the capability to divide can regain the capacity of the division under certain conditions; this phenomenon is called dedifferentiation. It occurs during secondary growth when permanent cell-like parenchyma regains the power of division to form vascular cambium and cork cambium. The redifferentiation is the event of losing the ability to divide by dedifferentiated cells.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:

questions.subject: Botany

In long day plants under short day conditions
In some short day and long day plants
In neither short day nor long day plants

Gibberellins, cause fruits like apple to elongate and improve its shape. They also delay senescence. Thus, the fruits can be left on the tree longer so as to extend the market period. Gibberellins also replace the long day requirement for flowering.

questions.subject: Botany

questions.solution: Abscisic acid (ABA) is a growth inhibitor, which is involved in seed dormancy. Dormant seeds germinate when ABA is overcome by gibberellins. ABA cause dormancy in axillary buds and acts as a Stress hormone in adverse environmental conditions.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The hormone involved in the metabolism of food material in cereal grain during germination is:
questions.solution:
Gibberellin is a class of plant growth regulators. This hormone was discovered from the fungus Gibberella fujikuroi (Class Deuteromycetes), whose perfect stage was assigned to Fusarium moniliforme. This fungus causes Bakanae disease or Bakane foolish seedling disease of rice. This causes rice plants to grow unusually taller, spindle-shaped, pale green in color and production of rice much lesser.
Chemically, gibberellin is gibbane-ring containing complex chemicals with vivid biological activities in plants. There are more than 30 gibberellins known so far. They all are acidic in nature and are called Gibberellic Acid (GA).
The main physiological role of GA includes:
1. Stem and internode elongation. Thus, by applying GA, a genetically dwarf plant can be made into a tall plant.
2. Inducing parthenocarpy for pome type fruits.
3. Help in overcoming natural dormancy in seeds, tubers, rhizomes, etc.
4. Controlling flowering in the long-day plants.
5. Production of male flowers in cannabis like plants.
6. Breakdown of sugar by activation of alpha-amylase in germinating barley seeds, which promotes germination. This is another characteristic property of GAs.

Auxin helps in increased protein synthesis, rhizogenesis, parthenocarpy induction, etc.

Cytokinins are a class of hormones that induce cell division, break apical dominance, expanding leaves, etc.

questions.solution: Indole acetic acid (IAA) and Indole butyric acid are natural auxin synthesized in plants. Naphthalene acetic acid and 2,4 dichlorophenoxy acetic acid are synthetic auxin. Auxin is mainly synthesized at shoot apex as light is necessary for the synthesis of auxin.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Bean seeds were planted and put on a sunny windowsill. As the plants grew, their stems bent toward the window. This bending was most likely caused by an
options: Unequal distribution of auxin in the stem.
Unequal distribution of a neurotransmitter in the stem.
Equal distribution of auxin in the stem.
Equal distribution of a neurotransmitter in the stem.

If the distribution were equal, the plant would grow just upwards. Neuro-transmitters are chemicals secreted by multicellular animals and are used in transmitting impulses in the nervous system.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match the column-I and column-II.
  Column-I   Column-II
(i) Auxin (A) Adenine derivatives
(ii) Gibberellin (B) Carotenoid derivatives
(iii) Cytokinin (C) Terpenes
(iv) ABA (D) Indole compounds
questions.solution:
Auxins are weakly acidic growth hormones having an unsaturated ring structure. Indole Acetic Acid (IAA) is the universal natural auxin derived from the precursor amino acid tryptophan with an indole ring structure. Auxins are produced in the stem tip and promotes cell elongation.

Gibberellins are weakly acidic, tetracyclic diterpenes with an ent-gibberelline (gibbane) ring structure formed from the precursors mevalonic acid or acetyl co-enzyme A. Gibberellins causes cell elongation of intact plants and increases the internodal length of dwarf plants. 

Cytokinins are plant hormones that are basic in nature and aminopurine (6-amino purine is adenine) or phenyl urea derivatives. Cytokinins promote the cell division or cytokinesis either alone or in conjugation with auxins.

Abscisic Acid (ABA) is a mild acidic dextrorotatory cis sesquiterpene growth hormone formed from the mevalonic acid or carotenoid xanthophylls.  ABA acts as a general growth inhibitor by counteracting other hormones like auxins, gibberellins and cytokinins.

questions.solution: In most higher plants, the growing apical bud inhibits growth of the lateral buds, a phenomenon called apical dominance and is induced by auxins like NAA, 2,4 D, IAA etc. Removal of shoot tips (decapitation) or addition of cytokinins like zeatin, kinetic etc., usually results in the growth of lateral buds. options: The hormone which also causes bolting in some plants
The hormone which is activated during deficiency of water
The hormone which is responsible for apical dominance
The hormone which prevents apical dominance is plants
questions.solution: The hormone which also causes bolting in some plants is Gibberellin. Gibberellins are growth promoters. They were first discovered in a fungus Gibberella fujikuroi. There are many gibberellins and they are denoted as GA1, GA2, GA3 and so on. However, GA3 was one of the first gibberellins to be discovered and remains the most intensively studied form. questions.q: The phytohormone responsible for increasing the shelf life of cut flowers and vegetables also helps in
options: Overcoming apical dominance and helps in sprouting of lateral buds
questions.solution: Apical dominance has been explained as due to the action of auxin present in the main apex. This view is amply supported by an experiment, where if the stem tip is cut off, the axillary buds found below sprout immediately. Instead, if an agar block containing auxin placed over the decapitated stem, the axillary buds remain suppressed. It is clear from the above experiment, that auxin present in the main apex somehow inhibits the growth of the axillary bud. The severity of apical dominance is greater on the axillary buds present nearer to the main apex. Suppression of growth of axillary buds by the presence of apical buds under the effect of hormone auxins.
Suppression of growth of axillary buds by the presence of apical buds under the effect of hormone cytokinins.

It adversely affects the fertility of the plant
The seeds cannot be stored under normal conditions for the next season

Such process occurs when the condition for the seed germination is favourable. Annual crop plants are those group that produce for only one growing season. For the next season the seeds of the plant are stored. If such plants slow vivipary then it will be not feasible to store seeds as the seeds have already germinated. questions.solution:
In arithmetic growth, the number of population increases by a constant number in each period. Their number goes on the increase with time. There is lag, log, and the stationary phase is present in the curve. In this curve, only one daughter cell divides and other daughter cells differentiate and mature. These characters are responsible for the linear curve in arithmetic growth.

In geometric growth, the growth is directly proportional to the nutrient supply. If we supply more nutrients then growth will occur. The sigmoid growth curve is also known as the logistic growth curve and it is S shape. In lag phase growth is slow and in the log phase, the growth increases very rapidly and in the last phase it slows down when they reach carrying capacity.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Internodal elongation is stimulated by:
questions.solution: Gibberellic acid (GA<sub>3</sub>) was one of the first gibberellins to be discovered and remains the most intensively studied form. All GAs are acidic. They produce a wide range of physiological responses in the plants. Their ability to cause an increase in length of axis is used to increase the length of grapes stalks. Gibberellins, cause fruits like apple to elongate and improve its shape. They also delay senescence. Thus, the fruits can be left on the tree longer so as to extend the market period. GA<sub>3</sub> is used to speed up the malting process in brewing industry. Sugarcane stores carbohydrate as sugar in their stems. Spraying sugarcane crop with gibberellins increases the length of the stem, thus increasing the yield by as much as 20 tonnes per acre. Spraying juvenile conifers with GAs hastens the maturity period, thus leading to early seed production. Gibberellins also promotes bolting (internode elongation just prior to flowering) in beet, cabbages and many plants with rosette habit.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Two leaves, A and B, are of different sizes but shows absolute increase in area in the unit time to give leaves A1 and B1 . Find out the absolute growth and relative growth rate of both the leaves.

questions.solution:
Growth rate is measured by increased growth per unit time. Growth in an organism or its part can occur in many different ways.

When the total growth of the living system is measured and compared in a particular unit time is referred as absolute growth rate. This growth rate is for that particular living system in that time interval and not compared with other living system.

Absolute growth = Growth in given time period = Growth (final time) - Growth (initial time)

Absolute growth of A = Growth A'-Growth A=10-5=5 cm2.

Absolute growth of B = Growth B'-Growth B=55-50=5 cm2 .

When the growth of living system measured per unit time is expressed on a common basis is referred to as relative growth rate. It is more of a comparative growth rate between initial time period and current time period.

Relative growth rate = Growth in given time/Initial growth*100

Relative growth rate A = (Final Growth - Initial Growth)/Initial Growth*

= (10-5)/5*100 = 100%

Relative growth rate B= (Final Growth - Initial Growth)/Initial Growth*

= (55-50)*100/50 = 10%

questions.solution: Some important food plants, wheat, barley, rye have two kinds of varieties: winter and spring varieties. They germinate, and over winter come out as small seedlings, resume growth in the spring, and are harvested usually around mid-summer.

questions.solution: Abscisic acid (ABA) was discovered for its role in regulating abscission and dormancy. But like other PGRs, it also has other wide ranging effects on plant growth and development. It acts as a general plant growth inhibitor and an inhibitor of plant metabolism. ABA inhibits seed germination. ABA stimulates the closure of stomata in the epidermis and increases the tolerance of plants to various kinds of stresses. Therefore, it is also called the stress hormone. ABA plays an important role in seed development, maturation and dormancy. By inducing dormancy, ABA helps seeds to withstand desiccation and other factors unfavourable for growth.

questions.subject: Botany

questions.solution:
Growth pattern of cell, organisms is uniform under favourable conditions & a typical growth curve in plants is sigmoidal. Thus following phases of growth are recognized.

(i) Lag phase: In lag period the growth is slow. It represents formative or cell division phase.

(ii) Log phase: Also called as exponential phase. During this phase growth is maximum & most rapid. It represents cell elongation phase.

(iii) Steady or stationary phase: It represents cell maturation phase.

Time taken in growth phases (mainly log phase) is called as grand period of growth.
