They require a continuous uninterrupted dark period for flowering and fail to flower if the dark period is interrupted by a brief flash of light.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Maturation phase of cell is characterized by:
questions.solution: Cells of maturation phase attains their maximal size in terms of wall thickening and protoplasmic modification. Cells in this phase becomes structurally and functionally specialized. Like xylem vessels loss protoplasm, endodermal cell wall gets deposited with suberin.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Recognize the figure and find out the CORRECT labeling.
options: a-elongation, c-differentiation, b-plasmatic growth, d-senescence, e-maturation
b-elongation, e-differentiation, a-plasmatic growth, c-senescence, d-maturation
a-elongation, d-differentiation, b-plasmatic growth, e-senescence, c-maturation
b-elongation, c- differentiation, a-plasmatic growth, e-senescence, d-maturation
questions.solution: The plant begins its life from the zygote. Plasmatic growth is a fundamental characteristic of living beings. Meristematic cells present at the apex that helps in increasing the length of the plant while the secondary meristem is responsible for increasing the girth of the plant. After the meristematic phase, an elongation phase is present in which cells get enlarged and results in new cell wall deposition. The maturation phase is present close to the elongation phase where cells reach a maximum size and protoplasmic modifications occur. Then cells differentiate to perform different functions. In this process, cells lose the ability of division. Later the senescence (death) of the cell occurs due to some environmental factors like drought or changing of the season.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: If a growing plant is decapitated
options: leaves become yellow and have a
questions.solution: The hormones which are produced in the plant are called phytohormone. Auxin is a phytohormone. An apical bud is present at the top of the plant and an axillary bud or lateral bud is present on the lateral side. The phytohormone which is synthesized in the apical bud is auxin that helps in maintaining the apical dominance in which the growth of the lateral bud stop but if the apical bud is decapitated, means removed then the concentration of the auxin gets low and this causes the activation of the axillary bud which helps in increasing the plant width.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Quantitative comparisons between the growth of the living system can be made in two ways:

(i) Measurement and the comparison of total growth per unit time is called the ....a.... growth rate.

(ii) The growth of the given system per unit time expressed on a common basis, eg.; per unit initial parameter is called ...b.... growth rate.
questions.solution: Quantitative comparisons between the growth of living system can also be made in two ways : (i) measurement and the comparison of total growth per unit time is called the absolute growth rate. (ii) The growth of the given system per unit time expressed on a common basis, e.g., per unit initial parameter is called the relative growth rate.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: During autumn, a boy notices that the road is littered with orange leaves. He looks up to find that the tree is devoid of most leaves, while some of them are still falling. The phytohormone responsible for this causes ________________.
options: development of carotenoids and dehiscence of leaves.
inhibits seed germination and promotes dormancy.
dessication of leaves and subsequent falling.
questions.solution: Abscisic acid stimulates senescence of leaves by causing destruction of chlorophyll and inhibition of protein and RNA synthesis. It acts as a general plant growth inhibitor and an inhibitor of plant metabolism. ABA inhibits seed germination. ABA stimulates the closure of stomata and increases the tolerance of plants to various kinds of stresses. Therefore, it is also called the stress hormone. ABA plays an important role in seed development, maturation and dormancy. By inducing dormancy, ABA helps seeds to withstand desiccation and other factors unfavourable for growth. In most situations, ABA acts as an antagonist to GAs.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The disease that is caused by fungal pathogen reported by E. Kurosawa in rice plant is:
questions.solution: The ‘bakanae’ (foolish seedling) disease of rice seedlings, was caused by a fungal pathogen Gibberella fujikuroi. E. Kurosawa (1926) reported the appearance of symptoms of the disease in rice seedlings when they were treated with sterile filtrates of the fungus. The active substances were later identified as gibberellic acid.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Apical dominance is caused by
questions.solution: The phenomenon where the later stems are suppressed in growth by the growth of the central stem is referred to as apical dominance. This occurs at the shoot tip due to the production of plant hormones. Plant hormones are chemicals that regulate the growth and development of the plant. The hormone that induces apical dominance is auxins and the hormone that break apical dominance is cytokinin.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Vernalisation is commonly seen in plants like __________, which are __________ in nature.
questions.solution: Another example of vernalisation is seen in biennial plants. Biennials are monocarpic plants that normally flower and die in the second season. Sugarbeet, cabbages, carrots are some of the common biennials. Subjecting the growing of a biennial plant to a cold treatment stimulates a subsequent photoperiodic flowering response.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Arithmetic growth rate can be mathematically expressed as:
questions.solution:
In arithmetic growth, following mitotic cell division, only one daughter cell continues to divide while the other differentiates and matures. The simplest expression of arithmetic growth is exemplified by a root elongating at a constant rate.
Mathematically, it is expressed as:
Lt = L0 + rt
Lt = length at time ‘t’
L0 = length at time ‘zero’
r = growth rate / elongation per unit time.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Plants which require the exposure to light for a period exceeding a well defined critical duration for flowering are called:
questions.solution: Plants require periodic exposure to light for flowering. Some plants need exposure for a period more than a well defined critical duration known as long-day plants and the other short-day plants are the ones which need exposure to light less than the well defined critical duration. Different plants have different critical duration. The day-neutral plants are the plants which show no correlation between exposure to the light duration and their flowering response.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Select the incorrect statement.
options: Growth, at a cellular level, is principally a consequence of increase in the amount of protoplasm.
In maize, the growth in root apical meristem growth as an increase in the size of the cell.
The growth of a pollen tube is measured in terms of its length.
An increase in surface area denotes the growth in a dorsiventral leaf.
questions.solution: In one single maize, root apical meristem can give rise to more than 17,500 new cells per hour, whereas cells in a watermelon may increase in size by up to 3,50,000 times. In the former, growth is expressed as increase in cell number; the latter expresses growth as increase in size of the cell. While the growth of a pollen tube is measured in terms of its length, an increase in surface area denotes the growth in a dorsiventral leaf.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The following figure shows:
options: Heterophylly in cotton, coriander and larkspur.
questions.solution: Every plant follows different pathways as a response to the environment, to form different structures, the ability to do so is called plasticity. Heterophylly in some plants is an example of the same. These plants have leaves that have a different shape when they are juvenile and the shape changes when they mature. The given figure depicts the heterophylly seen in larkspur when its juvenile and when they turn into an adult plant.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match the following (Column -I and Column II)
 
  Column-I   Column-II
a. Ethephon (i) GA
b. Genetic dwarfism (ii) Ethylene
c. Zeatin (iii) Natural auxin
d. IAA (iv) Cytokinin
questions.solution: Ethephon is used for the ripening of fruit. Indole-3-acetic acid is used as herbicide, its an auxin. Zeatin is a cytokinin derived from adenine. Genetic dwarfism can be removed by application of Gibberellins.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Biennials get changed into annuals by
questions.solution: Vernalization is a process in which the plants are exposed to certain periods of low temperature so that flowering can be induced in them. Biennials are plants that take two years to complete its life cycle. When these plants are subjected to artificial cold treatment and the correct temperature and photoperiods, they induce flowering in the first growing season itself, just like the annuals (biennials usually flower in the second year of their growing season).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Rapid inter-nodal elongation is caused due to which hormone?
questions.solution: Gibberellin promotes rapid intermodal elongation in genetically dwarf plants, this phenomenon is known as bolting. It also causes intermodal elongation in plants plant like sugarcane, thus is used to increase productivity of sugarcane.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Auxins are known to promote ____________ in pineapples.
questions.solution: Auxins help to initiate rooting in stem cuttings, an application widely used for plant propagation. Auxins promote flowering e.g. in pineapples. They help to prevent fruit and leaf drop at early stages but promote the abscission of older mature leaves and fruits.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Bakane disease leads to the discovery of which phytohormone (PGR)?
questions.solution: Phytohormone is plant hormones that are responsible for the growth and development of the plants. Some of them include gibberellic acid (GA), auxins, abscisic acid (ABA), cytokinins(CK), etc. Bakane disease also called the foolish seedling disease of rice, affects the rice plants, and is caused by the fungi Gibberella fujikuroi. The phytohormone, Gibberellins were first isolated from these fungi which caused the foolish seedling disease of rice plants and thus Bakane's disease led to the discovery of the plant hormone gibberellic acid (GA).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The hormone capable of replacing the requirement of long photoperiods for flowering is:
questions.solution: Gibberellic acid (GA3) was one of the first gibberellins to be discovered and remains the most intensively studied form. All GAs are acidic. They produce a wide range of physiological responses in the plants. Their ability to cause an increase in length of axis is used to increase the length of grapes stalks. Gibberellins, cause fruits like apple to elongate and improve its shape. They also delay senescence. Thus, the fruits can be left on the tree longer so as to extend the market period. GA3 is used to speed up the malting process in brewing industry. Sugarcane stores carbohydrate as sugar in their stems. Spraying sugarcane crop with gibberellins increases the length of the stem, thus increasing the yield by as much as 20 tonnes per acre. Spraying juvenile conifers with GAs hastens the maturity period, thus leading to early seed production. Gibberellins also promotes bolting (internode elongation just prior to flowering) in beet, cabbages and many plants with rosette habit.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The most delicate stage in the life cycle of an angiosperm where maximum mortality observed is the
questions.solution: Seed germination is the process where seed develops into a new plant by producing the shoot and root on germination. The germinated seed forms a young sporophyte called a seedling. It has plumule and radicle, where plumule forms the shoot bearing leaves and flower while the radicle forms the root part. Seedling stage is the most delicate stage of angiosperms and has high mortality rate due to drought condition been one of the main cause as roots are not able to maintain contact with soil sufficiently to prevent water stress.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Essential requirement for seed germination is
questions.solution: Germination is the process of growth of a plant that eventually causes the formation of a seedling. Many factors like temperature, water, oxygen regulate the process of germination. Seed is very durable and can germinate in a wide range of temperatures. Essential requirements for the germination process are water and oxygen and germination cannot occur take in their absence. Seeds need oxygen for aerobic respiration to produce energy.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Apical dominance can be overcome by:
questions.solution: In higher plants, the growing apical bud inhibits the growth of the lateral (axillary) buds, a phenomenon called apical dominance. Removal of shoot tips (decapitation) usually results in the growth of lateral buds. Cytokinins help overcome the apical dominance. They promote nutrient mobilisation which helps in the delay of leaf senescence.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements and find out the INCORRECT statement.

a. Plant growth is unique because plants retain the capacity for unlimited growth throughout their life.
b. Growth, at a cellular level, is principally a consequence of the increase in the amount of protoplasm.
c. One single maize root apical meristem can give rise to more than 3,50,000 new cells per hour, whereas cells in watermelon may increase in size by up to 17,500 times.
d. Environmental signals such as light, temperature and gravity also affect certain phases or stages of growth.
e. In geometric growth, following mitotic cell division, only one daughter cell continues to divide while the other differentiates and matures.
options: <math><mi mathvariant="normal">b</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi></math>

<math><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi></math>

<math><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></math>

<math><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></math>
questions.solution: In arithmetic growth, following mitotic cell division, only one daughter cell continues to divide while the other differentiates and matures. In geometrical growth, the initial growth is slow (lag phase), and it increases rapidly thereafter – at an exponential rate (log or exponential phase). One single maize root apical mersitem can give rise to more than 17,500 new cells per hour, whereas cells in a watermelon may increase in size by up to 3,50,000 times.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The cell-derived from meristems differentiates and regain the capacity to divide by a phenomenon called
questions.solution:
The cells derived from root apical and shoot-apical meristems and cambium differentiate and mature to perform specific functions. This act leading to maturation is termed as differentiation.

The living differentiated cells, that by now have lost the capacity to divide can regain the capacity of division under certain conditions. This phenomenon is termed as dedifferentiation.

While doing so, such meristems/tissues are able to divide and produce cells that once again lose the capacity to divide but mature to perform specific functions, i.e., get redifferentiated.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Growth can be measured in various ways. Which of these as to be used as parameters to measure growth?
questions.solution:
At the cellular level growth is due to an increase in the amount of protoplasm. However, it is difficult to measure the growth of protoplasm, but the protoplasm increase can be related to the increase in cell size, cell number, and cell size.

The quantitative growth can be measured in the increase in the fresh weight, dry weight, length, area, volume and cell number. The rate of growth is the growth per unit time and it is usually slow initially in early growth stages and later a rapid increase during the exponential phase is observed. A steady growth phase will be observed later with a decline phase.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In an experiment, one set of plants were exposed to 12 hr day and 12 hr night and the plants flowered. The other set with similar exposure to the day-night period but with a dark period interrupted by the flash of light did not produce the flower. Such a plant is referred to as
questions.solution: Every plant requires a certain amount of light and darkness to grow and this aspect is known as photoperiodism. The plants which require only a short period of darkness to flower are known as long-day plants whereas the plants which require a short day length and the long period of darkness without any interruption by light are known as short-day plants. Day-neutral plants are those which flower in which spectrum of the amount of light it receives. The intermediate type of plants is one which does not require long periods of darkness or light to flower.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Plant growth hormones extracted from a fungus and a fish are respectively
questions.solution: Gibberellins is the plant hormone that was produced from the fungus Gibberella fujikuroi after isolation and therefore the fungus is named gibberellin. This hormone is a plant growth regulator and is involved in stem elongation, dormancy, and various other processes involving plant growth. Kinetin is also a plant hormone that helps in plant growth by promoting cell division. This hormone was first isolated from the DNA of herring fish.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following plants requires light exposure less than the critical period to initiate flowering?
questions.solution: The critical photoperiod is the light period required for floral induction, which must not be exceeded in short-day plants and should always be exceeded in long day plants in order to bring them to flower. Tobacco is a short-day plant (SDP). When the photoperiod is less than the critical period plant will flower. Wheat, Spinach and oat are all long-day plants (LDP), which flower when they receive photoperiod or light hours above the critical photoperiod.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Which one of the PGRs would be used by farmers if they are asked to?

a Induce parthenocarpy in tomatoes

b Hastens fruit ripening in tomatoes and apples

c Induces flowering in mango

d Elongation and improvement in the shape of the apple

e Promote nutrient mobilization
options: a-auxins, b-ethephon, c-ethylene, d-GA, e- cytokinin
a-ethylene, b-GA, c-auxin, d - ethephon, e- cytokinin
a-cytokinin, b-auxin, c-GA, d-ethephon, e- ethylene
questions.solution:
Plant growth hormones are the signalling molecules that are produced in the plants in low concentrations. Parthenocarpy is the production of fruit artificially or naturally without fertilization of ovules.

Auxin is a plant hormone which when sprayed on the flowers of tomato induces parthenocarpy.

Ethephon is a plant growth regulator used for promotion of fruit ripening, abscission and to induce flowering in plants. Ethylene is the gaseous phytohormone responsible to induce flowering in mango plants as it is involved in the growth and senescence of leaves. GA is the gibberellic acid which is mainly involved in plant growth and development and therefore it is used for elongation and improvement in the shape of apple in plants. Cytokinin is a plant hormone primarily used to promote cell division, to overcome apical dominance and they also promote nutrient mobilization in addition to the formation of new leaves and chloroplast.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: One of the commonly used plant growth hormone in pineapple to promote flowering is
questions.solution: Indole-3-acetic acid (auxin) is a phytohormone which is generally produced by the growing apices of the stems and roots, from where they migrate to the regions of their action. It is observed that the growing apical bud inhibits the growth of the lateral (axillary) bud. Since apical meristem is the site of auxin synthesis, it is the physiological effect of the auxin which results in the phenomenon of apical dominance. Auxins promote flowering e.g. in pineapples. They help to prevent fruit and leaf drop at early stages but promote the abscission of older mature leaves and fruits.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Certain plants need to be exposed to a low temperature to hasten flowering later in life. This treatment is known as
questions.solution: Vernalisation is the phenomenon in which the flowering in plants is dependent on exposure to low temperatures. Vernalisation promotes flowering and enables the plant to have enough time to reach maturity. Stratification is a process which is used to break seed dormancy by providing it with the desirable conditions needed for the growth and scarification means braking of the tough exterior of the seed or weakening it to allow germination. Photoperiodism is the response of plants to the periods of day and night.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: One hormone helps in petiole elongation in deepwater rice plants, while the other stimulates closure of stomata. These are respectively:
questions.solution: The submerged rice water plants are unable to grow and elongate at times due to various reasons. Ethylene is a gaseous hormone which helps in the internode elongation or petiole elongation in plants. It is a multifunctional phytohormone which promotes or inhibits the growth and senescence of leaves depending on the plant species. ABA is abscisic acid which is known as an inhibitor and plays an important role in seed development and maturation by inducing the closure of stomata and also involved in seed dormancy.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The condition or process of deterioration with age is termed as _____.
questions.solution: Ageing of leaves is called senescence. It is the process of growing old, which occurs in all species and is typified by a gradual slowing down of metabolism and breakdown of tissues, often accompanied by endocrinal changes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match the following.
 
  ‘A’   ‘B’
(A) Auxin (I) Ripening and maturity of fruits
(B) Gibberellin (II) Differentiation of xylem elements
(C) Cytokinin (III) Prevention of genetic and physiological dwarfism
(D) Ethylene (IV) Found from tumour tissue of tobacco
questions.solution: Auxins are used for the differentiation of xylem elements, gibberellin is used for the removal of dwarfism and used for inter-nodal elongation. Cytokinin is a modified form of adenine and found in tumour cell of tobacco and used for overcoming apical dominance. Ethylene is a ripening hormone.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which hormone is obtained from herring sperm DNA?
questions.solution: Cytokinins are plant hormones that have specific effects on cytokinesis and cell division. These hormones were discovered as kinetin which was isolated from the autoclaved herring sperm DNA.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements and find out the INCORRECT statement.

a Both a short day plant and a long day plant can flower simultaneously in a given place.

b Sugar beet, cabbage, and carrot are common biennials.

c Some important food plants, wheat, barley, and rye have three kinds of varieties: winter, summer, and spring varieties.

d Vernalisation promotes precocious reproductive development late in the growing season and enables the plant to have sufficient time to reach maturity

e Many of the extrinsic factors such as temperature and light, control plant growth and development
options: <math><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">b</mi></math>

<math><mi mathvariant="normal">b</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi></math>

<math><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi></math>

<math><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></math>
questions.solution: The group of plants requiring less time of exposure to light are known as short-day plants whereas those which require longer duration are known as long-day plants, these plants can grow simultaneously in the same place. Vernalisation is a phenomenon which promotes flowering by preventing early reproductive development and giving the plants time to reach maturity. The food plants have two varieties, winter and spring. Vernalisation is also seen in biennials like sugarbeet, carrot and cabbage. The plant growth and development depends on many factors like temperature, light and water.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Mowing grass lawn facilitates better maintenance because:
options: Removal of apical dominance and stimulation of intercalary meristem
Removal of apical dominance and promotion of lateral meristem
questions.solution: Apical dominance is a common observation in vascular plants. If apical meristem is intact & growing, the lateral tips growth is suppressed. According to Thirnann & Skoog the Auxin, synthesized in apical meristem, in translocated downwards & inhibits the growth of lateral tips. That is why mowing -grass lawns facilitates better maintenance.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The hormone that promotes female flowers in cucumbers is:
questions.solution: Ethephon hastens fruit ripening in tomatoes and apples and accelerates abscission in flowers and fruits (thinning of cotton, cherry, walnut). It promotes female flowers in cucumbers thereby increasing the yield.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Dormancy of seeds is broken by ethylene, whereas it is induced by
questions.solution: Hormonal regulation may be a highly conserved mechanism of seed dormancy among seed plants. Induction and maintenance of seed dormancy by abscisic acid (ABA).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The phenomenon of induction of flowering upon low temperature treatment is known as?
questions.solution: There are plants for which flowering is either quantitatively or qualitatively dependent on exposure to low temperature. This phenomenon is termed vernalization. It prevents precocious reproductive development late in the growing season and enables the plant to have sufficient time to reach maturity. Vernalization refers specially to the promotion of flowering by a period of low temperature.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Environmental heterophylly is found in:
questions.solution: Plants follow different pathways in response to environment or phases of life to form different kinds of structures. This ability is called plasticity, e.g. heterophylly in cotton, coriander and larkspur. In such plants, the leaves of the juvenile plant are different in shape from those in mature plants. On the other hand, difference in shapes of leaves produced in air and those produced in water in buttercup also represent the heterophyllous development due to environment.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: One hormone hastens maturity period in juvenile conifers, a second hormone controls xylem differentiation, while the third hormone increases the tolerance of plants to various stresses. They are respectively:
questions.solution: Spraying juvenile conifers with gibberellins hastens their maturity period, thus leading to early seed production. Auxin controls xylem differentiation. Abscisic acid (ABA) increases the tolerance of plants to various kinds of stresses, therefore, is also known as the stress hormone.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In the 1950s, kinetin was first discovered by
questions.solution: F. Skoog and his co-workers observed that from the internodal segments of tobacco stems, the callus (a mass of undifferentiated cells) proliferated only if, in  addition to auxins the nutrients medium was supplemented with one of the following: extracts of vascular tissues, yeast extract, coconut milk or DNA. Miller et al. (1955), later identified and crystallised the cytokinesis promoting active substance that they termed kinetin.
